authors: Skye Leake;Alex M. Haberlie;Walker S. Ashley;James G. DiGilio Jr.;Anya Aponte;Brendan C. Wallace;Vittorio A. Gensini;Allison C. Michaelis
title: Distributions of Short‐Duration High‐Intensity Precipitation Events in the United States Under Intermediate and Pessimistic Climate Change Scenarios
abstract: Under a warming climate, the magnitude and frequency of intense precipitation are expected to increase globally, on average. However, changes in the regional variability of short‐duration high‐intensity (SDHI) precipitation across the contiguous United States—both temporally and spatially—remain uncertain, and most projections rest on resolutions too coarse to resolve the responsible processes. Herein, convection‐permitting, dynamically downscaled simulation output at 3.75 km grid spacing and 15‐min intervals is used to examine potential changes in the occurrence, accumulation, and magnitude of sub‐daily precipitation relative to simulated historical levels. Changes are concentrated at both tails of the intensity distribution: precipitation at or above the 99th $99\mathrm{t}\mathrm{h}$ percentile increases significantly in five of seven regions, exceeding 100% in the Northwest, while lighter intensities decrease by 10%–40%. These changes are regionally and seasonally concentrated rather than uniform, and their dependence on accumulation duration varies by region, so future hydroclimates may be characterized by fewer light‐to‐moderate events punctuated by more intense ones, a redistribution that will challenge water management and infrastructure design.

explanation: 该论文研究的是2024年5月的一次强太阳风暴对地球磁层的影响，涉及磁层顶和 cusps 的动力学变化，并使用软X射线成像技术进行模拟和分析。这与大气环境遥感技术中的卫星观测、磁层物理和太阳风相互作用等领域密切相关，因此与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）有强相关关系。

authors: J. Ng;L.‐J. Chen;B. Burkholder;D. Sibeck;F. S. Porter;K. H. Pham;V. G. Merkin;H. Connor;J. W. Bonnell;S. Petrinec;Y. Zou;B. Alterman;G. Cucho‐Padin
title: The May 2024 Storm: The Cusps and Dayside Magnetopause in Simulated Soft X‐Rays
abstract: The coronal mass ejection (CME) arriving at Earth on 10 May 2024 caused the most intense geomagnetic storm in the last two decades, resulting in highly unusual cusp and magnetopause dynamics. We simulate soft X‐Ray emission due to solar wind charge exchange with exospheric neutrals to image the global dayside dynamics, focusing on the impact of a dense CME current sheet during the storm main phase. The magnetopause moves inward to ∼4RE ${\sim} 4{R}_{E}$, and the cusps manifest as nearly parallel emission ridges in X‐Ray. As the interplanetary magnetic field reverses, the cusp ridges move apart to higher latitudes for ∼10 ${\sim} 10$ minutes after the reversal, addressing the open question of how the cusps evolve during and after northward turning of the IMF. Our work highlights soft X‐ray imaging enabling simultaneous observations of extreme solar‐wind impacts across multiple magnetospheric regions.

title: Subsurface Deformation and Recovery From the Ridgecrest Mw 7.1 Earthquake Revealed by P‐Wave Velocity Time‐Lapse Tomography
abstract: We investigate co‐ and post‐seismic P‐wave velocity (Vp) changes following the July 2019 Mw 7.1 Ridgecrest strike‐slip earthquake using time‐lapse tomography from 50,345 P‐wave arrivals (2011–2024). Co‐seismically, Vp changes correspond to the volumetric strain change lobes of the earthquake, increasing in compressional zones and decreasing in tensional zones. Post‐seismically, Vp changes exhibit a reverse pattern, suggesting ongoing subsurface recovery. Notably, the Coso volcanic field, although distal to the rupture, shows significant co‐seismic velocity reduction and rapid post‐seismic recovery, likely indicating fluid migration or poroelastic effects. These results reveal the complex mechanical and hydrological responses to co‐seismic stress changes and provide important insights into post‐seismic healing processes. Our findings offer robust seismic evidence for the response of material properties to crustal deformation, contributing to improved understanding of structure changes in the earthquake process.

title: Enhanced Melt Supply Promotes Near‐Symmetric Oceanic Crustal Accretion at the Ultraslow Eastern Gakkel Ridge
abstract: Variations in melt supply can shift slow and ultraslow ridges between magmatic and tectonic accretion modes, but whether this effect persists at Earth's slowest‐spreading ridge remains unclear. The eastern Gakkel Ridge provides a critical test because it spreads at only ∼6–10 mm/yr yet shows anomalously strong magmatism. We reconstruct sediment thickness and residual basement across the Eurasian Basin using seismic constraints and time‐dependent sedimentation models for the poorly constrained eastern Nansen Basin. Most of the western Eurasian Basin shows deep residual basement and variable flank asymmetry, consistent with magma‐poor ultraslow accretion. Eastward, residual basement becomes progressively shallower and more symmetric. In the eastern Nansen Basin, shallow residual basement persists even under maximum sedimentation, indicating sustained crustal thickening on both conjugate flanks since ∼45 Ma. These results show that enhanced melt supply can shift oceanic crustal accretion toward a near‐symmetric, magma‐dominated mode even at Earth's slowest‐spreading ridge.

title: Gamma‐Ray Glows Commonly Followed by Lightning: A Statistical Study of the Spatio‐Temporal Relationship
abstract: Gamma‐ray glows are prolonged enhancements of gamma rays from thunderclouds, which are often linked to large‐scale electric fields rather than individual lightning. The link between glows and lightning remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed 300 glows observed during the ALOFT aircraft campaign and optical lightning detected by GLM. The results indicate that lightning becomes progressively less likely to coexist with a glow as the gamma‐ray intensity increases. Lightning activity also decreases several seconds before the glow peak but increases sharply afterward. Furthermore, approximately 78% of glows are followed by lightning within 1 s and 10 km, and the lightning frequency during the following second is 5.3 times that during the preceding second. These results reveal that lightning is closely related to glow reduction, suggesting that glow‐producing high‐field conditions and lightning discharge are closely coupled in the evolution of the thunderstorm electrical environment.

authors: Keisuke Yoshida;Satoshi Ide;Yihe Huang
title: Multi‐Scale Growth of an Mw 7.0 Earthquake via Hierarchical Cascading Rupture From an Mw 3.8 Repeating Event
abstract: To understand what governs earthquake size, we investigated the 2021 Mw 7.0 Japan Trench earthquake, which began near a nest of repeating earthquakes. High‐precision hypocenter relocation and P‐waveform correlation show that the mainshock initiated nearly identically to Mw 3.8 repeaters. Waveform deconvolution reveals that, after breaking the Mw 3.8 patch within 0.1 s, the mainshock rupture cascaded through Mw 5–6 patches within 2 s and into the main slip area at 3–6 s. Four preceding Mw 5.1–6.1 events, some with higher initial moment rates, did not rupture this main area, likely because the locked region remained too far from failure. Their repeated occurrence may reflect progressive unlocking of this region. In 2021, a start nearly identical to Mw 3.8 repeaters cascaded hierarchically into an Mw 7.0 rupture, suggesting that earthquake size depends less on how rupture begins than on whether surrounding locked regions are ready to fail.

authors: Peng Liang;Shurui Gu;Xinming Du;Hangyi Zhao;Haixia Gu;Kailun Pan;Xiaoping Yang
title: Dune Crestline Mapping With Deep Learning Reveals Large‐Scale Dune Patterns in NW China
abstract: Dune crestlines encode sediment transport dynamics and atmospheric forcing, yet their large‐scale quantification has been constrained by labor‐intensive mapping or limited resolution. Here we develop an attention‐augmented U‐Net model to automatically extract crestlines from ∼1 m resolution satellite imagery. Trained on 17,798 manually annotated crestlines, the model maps over 4 million crest features across the Badain Jaran and Tengger Deserts, yielding an unprecedented high‐resolution data set of dune‐field organization. Integrating ERA5‐Land wind reanalysis and Copernicus digital elevation model‐derived equivalent sand thickness, we quantify spatial variations in crest orientation, spacing, sinuosity, and hierarchy with respect to boundary conditions. Crest orientations largely agree with predictions from the bed‐instability mode under sand‐covered conditions, while deviations near upwind margins and transport corridors indicate elongation‐mode preference under sand‐starved bed. A downwind reduction in orientation dispersion and sinuosity reveals system‐scale reorganization driven by directional filtering through a narrow transport corridor, highlighting coupled wind‐sediment controls on self‐organized dune fields.

authors: Caiyi Fei;Maodong Yan;Jiuhou Lei
title: A Study of Kelvin‐Helmholtz Instability at Unmagnetized Planets by Finite Larmor Radius MHD
abstract: Kelvin–Helmholtz instability (KHI) at unmagnetized planetary ionopauses plays a key role in driving solar wind–ionosphere coupling and planetary ion escape. We investigate KHI using a two‐dimensional finite Larmor radius (FLR) MHD model. The FLR effect produces hemispheric asymmetry: the sign of Ω⋅B $\boldsymbol{\Omega }\cdot \mathbf{B}$, where B $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field and Ω=∇×v $\boldsymbol{\Omega }=\nabla \times \mathbf{v}$ is the vorticity, determines whether KHI is enhanced or suppressed. During nonlinear evolution, the FLR effect suppresses secondary instabilities and turbulent mixing. Long‐wavelength vortices detach as plasma blobs, whereas short‐wavelength vortices remain attached, sharply reducing ion escape. The preferred hemisphere also depends on ionospheric magnetic‐field strength. Under strong fields, KHI develops preferentially for Ω⋅B>0 $\boldsymbol{\Omega }\cdot \mathbf{B} > 0$; as the field weakens, the growth rates cross and Ω⋅B<0 $\boldsymbol{\Omega }\cdot \mathbf{B}<  0$ becomes dominant. These results highlight ion gyro‐motion as an important control on hemispheric asymmetry and plasma loss at unmagnetized planetary boundaries.

title: On the Stability and Sensitivity of Climate‐Informed Flood Frequency Models
abstract: Reliable flood change projections under climate change are critical for water resources planning yet remain challenging due to uncertainty in climate‐informed statistical models. Conventional approaches relate flood distribution parameters to climate variables using log‐linear formulations, which can produce unrealistically large flood estimates. In this study, we develop a semi‐parametric statistical framework that constrains flood variability using a bounded logistic link function and estimates parameters from hydroclimatically analogous samples. Using 548 natural basins across the coterminous United States, we evaluate the proposed approach against log‐linear formulations from the entire sample. Model performances are assessed based on both the accuracy and sensitivity of flood quantiles to climate forcings. Results show that the proposed framework yields more stable and realistic flood quantile estimates, particularly under high precipitation conditions, and better preserves flood sensitivity. These findings highlight the value of bounded, locally informed statistical models for robust flood risk assessment under climate change.

authors: Shu Xu;Lili Xia;Alan Robock;Charles Bardeen;Simchan Yook;Sasha Madronich;Soko Setoguchi
title: Impacts of Nuclear War on Human Health From Changed Surface Ultraviolet Radiation
abstract: Climate model simulations indicate that surface ultraviolet (UV) radiation would change after soot injection into the stratosphere during a nuclear war, due to the competing effects of ozone depletion and aerosol attenuation. Using climate model simulations, we evaluate UV impacts under two scenarios: a regional India‐Pakistan conflict producing 5 Tg of soot and a global U.S.‐Russia war producing 150 Tg. UV enhancements due to ozone depletion substantially shorten safe outdoor exposure time, particularly for individuals with lighter skin types. Applying UV dose‐response relationships to the year 2000 population data, without accounting for direct conflict mortality or famine‐related population loss, the 5 Tg scenarios result in approximately 5,300–9,800 additional skin cancer deaths within 10–15 years and up to 75,000 cumulative excess deaths over the following century. In contrast, strong aerosol attenuation under the 150 Tg scenario initially suppresses surface UV, resulting in about 8,500 fewer skin cancer deaths within 15 years and a maximum cumulative reduction of approximately 17,000 deaths over the following century. These findings demonstrate that nuclear war‐induced changes in surface UV radiation represent a persistent but previously understudied health impact of nuclear war. While skin cancer would not dominate overall mortality following a nuclear war, enhanced cumulative surface UV radiation represents an additional, long‐lasting threat to human health that compounds other global impacts such as climate disruption and food insecurity. The excess UV may also pose negative impacts on animals and plants, including those used for agriculture, which remain to be quantified.

title: ctDNA clearance and outcomes for resectable lung cancer from NeoCOAST-2
abstract:
ctDNA clearance and outcomes for resectable lung cancer from NeoCOAST-2 
 Patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain at high risk of relapse despite perioperative treatment1-3. NeoCOAST-2 (NCT05061550), a phase 2, randomised platform trial, tested novel perioperative treatments in patients with stage IIA–IIIB NSCLC. At primary analysis, combining standard chemotherapy plus durvalumab (anti-PD-L1 antibody) with oleclumab (Arm 1, n = 76), monalizumab (Arm 2, n = 72) or datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd; Arm 4, n = 54) resulted in pathological complete response (pCR) rates of 20.3%, 25.7%, and 35.2%, respectively4. Here, we present the first report of prespecified secondary endpoints of event-free survival (EFS) and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) clearance, and exploratory analyses of associations between ctDNA dynamics and clinical outcomes. The 24-month EFS rates were 70.5%, 75.7% and 77.9% in Arms 1, 2 and 4, respectively. Using a tumour-agnostic assay, ctDNA clearance at neoadjuvant Cycle 3 Day 1 was highest in Arm 4 (50.9%, 54.5%, and 72.5% in each arm, respectively). ctDNA clearance correlated with prolonged EFS versus non-clearance (pooled hazard ratio (HR) 0.22; 95% CI = 0.11–0.45, P = 0.0000443). Patients with both ctDNA clearance and pCR had favourable EFS outcomes versus those with neither (EFS HR 0.10, 95% CI = 0.02–0.42, P = 0.002). These findings suggest combined assessment of ctDNA clearance and pCR may improve risk stratification, and that the numerically highest pCR4 and EFS rates with the Dato-DXd combination warrant further evaluation.

title: Holographic focused ultrasound enables multitarget EV and MSC delivery for neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke
abstract:
Noninvasive multitarget delivery to peri-infarct regions after ischemic stroke remains challenging. Here, authors use holographic focused ultrasound to deliver EVs and MSCs to infarct borders, promoting neurovascular repair in mice. 
 Noninvasive multitarget delivery of size-diverse therapeutics, including extracellular vesicles (EVs) and mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), to peri-infarct zones is hindered by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and heterogeneous infarct topographies. Here, we developed a hologram-assisted multitarget BBB opening (HaMBO) platform combining low-cost 3D-printed holograms with a single-element ultrasound transducer. Spatially tailored acoustic fields enabled localized BBB opening along infarct borders. In male mice with transient focal cerebral ischemia, a single two-minute HaMBO treatment safely enhanced the peri-infarct delivery of EVs and MSCs, reduced brain atrophy by ~56%, increased angiogenesis by ~2-fold and neural progenitor proliferation by ~4-fold, and improved long-term behavioral recovery. Spatial transcriptomic analysis associated HaMBO-assisted EV therapy with reduced macrophage infiltration and enhanced pro-angiogenic and neurogenic signaling. Human skull-based simulations further demonstrated HaMBO’s clinical adaptability across diverse stroke scenarios. Thus, HaMBO provides a safe, low-cost, and customizable platform for noninvasive multitarget delivery in ischemic stroke and other neurological disorders. explanation: 该论文研究的是脑内方向细胞（head direction cells）如何受头部固定和行为状态的影响，属于神经科学领域，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）无关。
authors: Alexandr Pak;Janna Aarse;Heng Wei Zhu;Jean-Paul Noel;Simón Carrillo Segura;André A. Fenton;Dora Angelaki
title: Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice
abstract:
Head direction cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nuclei provide a compass-like signal in the brain. Here, the authors investigate how head fixation and behavioural state impact head-direction attractor dynamics. 
 Head direction (HD) cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nucleus form the brain’s internal compass, and are often modeled as a ring attractor maintaining azimuth coding by leveraging continuous visual and inertial sensory input. Here, we test how the common experimental preparation of head-fixed animals alters this code. Complete head-fixation that creates vestibular conflict disrupts both unit and population encoding of head direction, while selectively constraining head-on-body movements either in real or virtual reality uniquely impairs HD population activity. More specifically, attractor dynamics are altered in head-restrained male mice during periods of immobility, and a computational model recapitulates this effect by perturbing lateral connectivity among HD neurons. These dynamics recover several hundred milliseconds prior to locomotion onset, suggesting that an efference copy or prediction of a re-afferent signal is necessary to maintain HD network activity during head restraint. More generally, the results indicate that the HD network is a context- and state-dependent predictive estimator, stabilized by forthcoming self-motion signals. The classic ring-attractor models should be revised to integrate context-dependent dynamics with prospective motor signals, offering a more complete account of how the brain’s compass remains stable across both naturalistic and constrained conditions. authors: Xiao Gu;Yukang Zhang;Shaojun You;Zhenchu Fu;Bo Ni;Jianhua Chang;Haibin Ni;Xiaoshuang Chen;Wei Lu;Guanhai Li;Lujun Huang
title: Dual-point-groups engineering enable multi-ultrahigh-Q resonances via Brillouin zone folding in tetramer metasurfaces
abstract:
A dual-point group framework of constructing multiple ultrahigh-Q resonances within tetramer metasurfaces with a C4v symmetry via Brillouin zone folding is developed, enabling high-performance nanophotonic devices like sum frequency generation and laser. 
 High-Q resonances based on bound states in the continuum provide a central route of enhancing light-matter interactions. Here, we present a dual-point group framework of constructing multiple ultrahigh-Q resonances within tetramer metasurfaces with a C4v symmetry via Brillouin zone folding. By selectively preserving or reducing the O- and S-group symmetries of super lattice, guided modes below light cone can be converted into guided resonances or bound states in the continuum with controlled degeneracy lifting, Q-factor scaling, eigenfield profiles, and mode splitting. Besides, applying rectangular lattice provides an alternative way of tuning the Q-factors and mode splitting. Finally, we experimentally demonstrate such two types of high-Q resonances in the tetramer metasurfaces. Measurement results show that the mode splitting can be tuned from 0 nm to 70 nm while the Q-factors are modulated from 300 to 20,000 by varying the asymmetry parameters. This work establishes a symmetry-addressed route for programmable multi-resonant high-Q metasurfaces. A dual-point group framework of constructing multiple ultrahigh-Q resonances within tetramer metasurfaces with a C4v symmetry via Brillouin zone folding is developed, enabling high-performance nanophotonic devices like sum frequency generation and laser.

explanation: 该论文主要讨论的是扩散模型（diffusion models）和密集关联记忆（dense associative memory）理论，涉及的是人工智能和机器学习领域中的生成模型和记忆检索问题，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演等）没有直接关系。
authors: Bao Pham;Gabriel Raya;Matteo Negri;Mohammed J. Zaki;Luca Ambrogioni;Dmitry Krotov
title: Emergence of diffusion models from associative memory through memorization and generalization
abstract:
Viewing Diffusion Models through the lens of Dense Associative Memory theory reveals that spurious states, traditionally viewed as memory errors, are in fact a critical intermediate phase of generalization. Here, authors demonstrate their existence across a wide range of architectures and datasets. 
 Dense Associative Memories (DenseAMs) are generalizations of Hopfield networks that store training data at local minima of the energy landscape. When the amount of training data exceeds the critical memory storage capacity, new local minima (different from the training data) emerge. These emergent local minima, known as spurious states, can hinder memory retrieval. We examine diffusion models (DMs) through the DenseAM lens, viewing their generative process as an attempt of a memory retrieval. In the small data regime, DMs create distinct attractors for each training sample, akin to DenseAMs below the critical capacity. As the training set size increases, DMs transition to generalization. We identify a critical intermediate phase, predicted by DenseAM theory, characterized by the emergence of spurious states. In generative modeling, these previously overlooked states are no longer negative artifacts but rather are the first signs of generative capabilities. Their existence is demonstrated across a wide range of architectures and datasets. Viewing Diffusion Models through the lens of Dense Associative Memory theory reveals that spurious states, traditionally viewed as memory errors, are in fact a critical intermediate phase of generalization. Here, authors demonstrate their existence across a wide range of architectures and datasets.

title: NYNRIN safeguards leukemia stem cells by sustaining thioredoxin activity to maintain redox homeostasis
abstract:
In patients with acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), the presence of leukaemic stem cells (LSCs) promotes resistance to therapy and is associated with poor prognosis. Here, the authors demonstrate that NYNRIN protects LSCs from oxidative stress by maintaining thioredoxin activity, identifying NYNRIN as a potential therapeutic target in AML. 
 Leukemia stem cells (LSCs) primarily rely on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) for energy production, a metabolic feature that inevitably generates excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). NYNRIN (NYN domain and retroviral integrase containing) is highly expressed in LSC-like cells and is associated with poor prognosis in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Genetic targeting of NYNRIN impairs LSC-like cell maintenance and in vivo leukemogenic capacity in MLL-AF9- and HOXA9/MEIS1-driven AML models, and compromises the in vivo pathogenicity of patient-derived LSC-like cells. Mechanistically, NYNRIN sustains thioredoxin (Trx) activity by functioning as an RNA-binding protein that directly binds and degrades TXNIP mRNA via its NYN domain. Loss of NYNRIN stabilizes TXNIP mRNA, leading to TXNIP accumulation, which disrupts Trx-mediated redox buffering, induces ROS overproduction and mitochondrial dysfunction, and triggers LSC apoptosis. Notably, NYNRIN inhibition potentiates venetoclax efficacy by compromising Trx-mediated ROS clearance, lowering the apoptotic threshold of LSCs. Collectively, our findings reveal a critical NYNRIN-TXNIP-Trx axis that safeguards LSCs by enabling efficient ROS clearance. In patients with acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), the presence of leukaemic stem cells (LSCs) promotes resistance to therapy and is associated with poor prognosis. Here, the authors demonstrate that NYNRIN protects LSCs from oxidative stress by maintaining thioredoxin activity, identifying NYNRIN as a potential therapeutic target in AML.

title: Evaluating anonymized genome re-identification using polygenic predictions and its implications for data privacy
abstract:
Although anonymized genomes can in principle be re-identified by predicting traits through Polygenic Scores, the authors show that in realistic settings the risk is negligible, alleviating privacy concerns around sharing anonymized genomes. 
 Re-identification by phenotypic prediction aims to determine whether a genome belongs to a specific individual by comparing the individual’s known traits with those predicted from the genome. Although this tracing attack is widely discussed in the genomic privacy literature, its practical risk remains uncertain. As genome-wide association studies (GWAS) continue to improve phenotypic prediction, concerns about the potential for this attack increase. Here, to quantify its real-world threat, we develop a probabilistic framework that estimates the likelihood of a match between an individual’s observed traits and polygenic scores (PGS) derived from a genome, while accounting for prediction accuracy and genetic and environmental correlations between traits. We benchmark this re-identification method and examine how the prior probability that a random genome and set of traits correspond to the same person affects performance. Finally, we assess whether sensitive genetic information, such as APOE-ε4 status (linked with Alzheimer’s disease) can be inferred through this attack. Our method outperforms a state-of-the-art tool, reaching a precision above 99% for a recall of 40% when considering a prior of 50%. However, in real-world settings, we estimate that realistic priors do not exceed 4 × 10−4%, resulting in a precision lower than 0.13% at the same recall. Inference of sensitive genetic variants also proves ineffective: precision above 50% for identifying APOE-ε4 carriers is achieved only at a recall below 20%. Thus, although re-identification by phenotypic prediction is technically feasible, its effectiveness in real-world conditions remains limited. Although anonymized genomes can in principle be re-identified by predicting traits through Polygenic Scores, the authors show that in realistic settings the risk is negligible, alleviating privacy concerns around sharing anonymized genomes.

title: Spatiotemporal proteomics reveals dynamic antiparallel gradients shaping signalling waves
abstract:
Researchers map rhythmic protein changes in developing mouse embryos and reveal how dynamic, antiparallel RSPO3 and LGR4 patterns shape signalling waves that control the formation of body segments contributing to the spine. 
 Embryonic development is driven by dynamic protein networks, yet how these dynamics shape morphogenesis remains poorly understood. Somitogenesis, the rhythmic segmentation of vertebrate embryos, is controlled by signalling gradients and oscillations in the presomitic mesoderm (PSM), but the underlying protein dynamics remain largely unknown. Here, we combine microfluidic synchronisation of mouse embryo tails with quantitative proteomics and transcriptomics to resolve spatiotemporal protein dynamics during somitogenesis. We identify proteins with dynamic expression during somitogenesis and reveal an antiparallel, dynamic R-Spondin/LGR signalling pattern that explains how Wnt oscillation amplitude increases despite declining Wnt ligand levels in the anterior PSM. Dynamic ligand expression is validated in mouse gastruloids, and perturbation of ligand dynamics reduces oscillation amplitude and impairs somite formation. Together, our findings identify R-Spondin as a dynamic amplifier of Wnt signalling oscillations and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how protein dynamics regulate mammalian tissue patterning. title: Complementary axes of functional system integrity and integration with divergent clinical correlates characterize focal epilepsy
abstract:
Zhang and colleagues identify two complementary aspects of brain network topology in focal epilepsy, with system integrity showing modest preferential associations with cognition and system integration with clinical features. 
 Focal epilepsy affects distributed brain systems, yet characterizations of patient-specific network organization that are clinically meaningful remain limited. Using resting-state functional MRI, we estimated overlapping individualized networks and derived two complementary axes (1) network correspondence, indexing system integrity through canonical system expression, and (2) k-hubness, indexing cross-system integration through multi-network participation. We studied a presurgical cohort of 305 patients with focal epilepsy and 224 healthy participants and an independent validation cohort of 903 patients spanning focal and common generalized and childhood epilepsy syndromes and 666 healthy participants. Correspondence disruption was broadly shared across focal epilepsies, whereas k-hubness alterations showed lateralized and syndrome-dependent redistributions of cross-system integration. The axes shared variance but showed modest preferential associations, with correspondence relating to cognition and k-hubness to epilepsy clinical features. Together, these measures characterize common and heterogeneous alterations in individualized brain system organization, linking complementary aspects of network topology to cognitive and clinical variation. Zhang and colleagues identify two complementary aspects of brain network topology in focal epilepsy, with system integrity showing modest preferential associations with cognition and system integration with clinical features.

title: A circular oligo(disulfide) anolyte enables practical aqueous redox flow batteries
abstract:
Aqueous flow batteries are ideal for grid storage but lack sustainable, high-capacity anolytes. Here the authors report a recyclable oligo(disulfide) design that combines closed-loop recyclability with good electrochemical performance. 
 Aqueous redox flow batteries are promising for large-scale grid energy storage, but their widespread implementation is hindered by the lack of anolyte materials that combine high capacity, environmental compatibility, recyclability, low cost and long-term stability. While organic anolyte molecules offer a potential sustainable solution, integrating these competing attributes within a single molecular platform remains challenging. Here we report a recyclable oligo(disulfide)-based anolyte in which robust sulfur–sulfur bonds serve as redox-active sites. The anolyte is synthesized by ring-opening polymerization of potassium-form endogenous thioctic acid, providing a scalable route to high-concentration redox-active species. Paired with a sulfonated cobalt phthalocyanine catalyst, this oligo(disulfide) anolyte delivers a capacity density of 128 Ah l−1 with a 95.5% material utilization rate at 50 mA cm−2. Using a carbon-coated sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) membrane with a sulfur–sulfur bond concentration of 0.25 M, the battery retains 98.1% of its capacity over 2,200 cycles while maintaining an energy efficiency of approximately 70% at 100 mA cm−2. We further validate the scalability and closed-loop recyclability of this chemistry in a 63 Wh stack. Our findings establish oligo(disulfide)s as a robust, circular redox platform, providing a pathway towards more resource-efficient and sustainable grid-scale energy storage. Here the authors report a recyclable oligo(disulfide) design that combines closed-loop recyclability with good electrochemical performance.

title: Efficient carbon dioxide separation with molecularly thin bilayer carbon membranes
abstract:
Membrane-based separations offer a promising energy-efficient approach to mitigating CO2 emissions. Here the authors develop molecularly thin graphene–amorphous carbon membranes that simultaneously deliver sharp molecular sieving, high permeance and mechanical stability for selective CO2 separation. 
 As an energy-efficient and scalable alternative to conventional chemical absorption, membrane-based carbon capture requires materials that simultaneously combine molecular-level thinness, precise sub-nanometre porosity and exceptional mechanical robustness—a longstanding trilemma in separation science. Here we report graphene–amorphous carbon bilayer membranes that overcome these trade-offs by way of a graphene-guided polymer conversion approach. Leveraging a super-spreading effect, we coat graphene with a uniform, ultra-smooth, polymer-derived carbon layer as thin as 2 nm, achieving a high Young’s modulus of approximately 26.8 GPa. Controlled pyrolysis of the polymer precursor generates a carbon network featuring narrowly distributed, high-precision ultramicropores. The resulting graphene–amorphous carbon membranes exhibit sharp molecular sieving (selectivity of >60 for CO2/N2, >70 for H2/CO2 and >70 for CO2/CH4) alongside an exceptional CO2 permeance of up to 5,000 gas permeation units that surpasses existing benchmarks. This combination of structural integrity and separation performance enables efficient carbon capture across varied flue gas, syngas and natural gas streams, establishing graphene–amorphous carbon membranes as a versatile, energy-efficient platform for sustainable molecular separations. Membrane-based separations offer a promising energy-efficient approach to mitigating CO2 emissions. Here the authors develop molecularly thin graphene–amorphous carbon membranes that simultaneously deliver sharp molecular sieving, high permeance and mechanical stability for selective CO2 separation.

title: Monsoon-driven dry-wet seasonal contrast reveals mitigation opportunity for methane emissions in South Asia
abstract:
Monsoon-driven dry-wet seasonal contrast reveals mitigation opportunity for methane emissions in South Asia 
 South Asia is a global methane (CH4) hotspot with strong monsoon-driven seasonality, yet wet-season emissions remain poorly constrained due to persistent cloudiness. Here we quantify dry- and wet-season methane emissions separately over South Asia during 2019–2024 using TROPOMI-constrained analytical inversions. By leveraging satellite observations from downwind regions, we are able to effectively constrain wet-season emissions despite sparse coverage. Anthropogenic sources dominate the regional total, accounting for 77.2% (28.8 Tg a−1; interannual range: 25.3–30.9 Tg a⁻¹), with major contributions from livestock (35.0% (32.9%–36.0%)), rice cultivation (21.8% (20.4%–23.1%)), and waste management (13.8% (12.4%–14.5%)). Six-year mean wet-season emissions (49.9(44.6–53.4) Tg a-1) are nearly twice dry season emissions (28.2(23.8–33.6) Tg a−1), driven by wetlands (5.5×), rice (2.6×), waste management (1.2×), and fossil fuels (1.2×); seasonality in waste and fossil fuels emissions is however missing from current inventories. Furthermore, latest national reports underestimate India’s methane emissions partly by neglecting seasonal variability. Despite much larger wet-season emissions, dry-season livestock and waste, unexpectedly, dominate interannual variability, likely indicating sensitivity to climate anomalies and potential implications for climate-resilient mitigation. South Asia contributed substantially to global methane surge in 2021, but not 2020. Our findings underpin previously-overlooked mitigation priorities that vary sharply by season.

title: The dryness control of MJO emergence
abstract:
The dryness control of MJO emergence 
 Despite decades of researches into the Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO) dynamics, the mechanisms of the MJO initiation from the eastern Africa–western Indian Ocean remain a major barrier to subseasonal predictions. Here, we identify a unique controlling effect on the MJO emergence by the preceding suppressed convection over the Indian Ocean (IOSC) and western Pacific (WPSC) that likely originates from Southern-hemisphere wave trains. A topographic pathway is tactfully revealed: East-African highlands force southerly transitions via the mechanical blocking of equatorial westerlies responding to an anomalous convective pattern. Consequently, moist air is advected from equatorial Africa to fuel the MJO emergence. Ensemble high-resolution simulations confirm this hidden topographic link. Moreover, the IOSC flattens the background moisture gradient over the Indian Ocean, while the WPSC introduces anomalous westerlies due to its westward propagation, both lowering the efficiency of the horizontal moisture advection in initiating the MJO. These findings advance our understanding of MJO genesis pathways from perspectives of topographic-link and moisture sources over equatorial Africa.

abstract:
Climate conditions in 2023 were exceptionally warm globally. Armenia experienced exceptionally high temperatures in March, November and December 2023, resulting in an extremely low mountain snowpack. Advective processes associated with meridional (in March) and zonal (November-December) flows were dominant large-scale factors producing strong positive temperature anomalies across Armenia. title: Traffic and combustion emission controls leave cooking as a dominant local source of primary PM<sub>1</sub> in megacities
abstract:
Traffic and combustion emission controls leave cooking as a dominant local source of primary PM<sub>1</sub> in megacities 
 Megacities frequently suffer from poor air quality, with PM2.5 concentrations routinely exceeding WHO guidelines and elevating the risk of cardiovascular and respiratory disease. Air quality legislation typically targets primary emissions from traffic, a dominant urban source of PM₂.₅. Here, we present direct, chemically resolved quantification of PM₁ emissions from three contrasting megacity neighbourhoods—London, Beijing and Delhi—revealing the magnitude and diversity of urban sources by applying a novel source attribution approach to eddy-covariance flux measurements using aerosol mass spectrometry. In Delhi, traffic and combustion dominate primary PM₁ emissions. In contrast, cooking is the largest source during mealtimes in London and Beijing, contributing up to 83% of midday emissions and 87% in the early evening in London, and up to 61% and 76%, respectively, in Beijing. These findings suggest that air quality legislation in London and Beijing has effectively reduced non-refractory transport and combustion emissions, allowing cooking to emerge as the largest local source of primary non-refractory PM₁. Although cooking is not included in national, European or global emission inventories, recent estimates from the London Atmospheric Emissions Inventory align well with our observations. Together, these results show that the sources dominating primary non-refractory PM₁ emissions differ from those controlling ambient PM1 mass. Although cooking is now the leading primary source in London and Beijing, further reductions in urban PM₁ will depend on mitigating secondary formation processes.

title: A snow-jet bridging mechanism driving the Afro-Asian summer monsoon precipitation dipole
abstract:
A snow-jet bridging mechanism driving the Afro-Asian summer monsoon precipitation dipole 
 The Afro-Asian summer monsoon precipitation sustains billions of people across the two continents, and its variability strongly affects water supply, irrigation, and drought-flood risks. While this variability has been linked to air-sea interactions, its connection with land-surface signals remains unclear. Using large-ensemble snow perturbation experiments and information flow causal analysis, we show that reduced Tibetan Plateau snow cover (TPS) contributes to a dipole pattern in Afro-Asian summer monsoon precipitation: positive anomalies over tropical Africa and negative anomalies over South Asia. This relationship is modulated by an accelerated tropical easterly jet (TEJ). Reduced TPS enhances thermal heating, exciting an upper-level anticyclonic anomaly. The easterly flow along its southern flank intensifies the TEJ, enhancing moisture transport toward tropical Africa and reinforcing the low-level anticyclonic anomaly over South Asia, resulting in a dipole precipitation pattern. Since 2006, TPS extent has stayed below 9% (a transition after which the TPS-TEJ coupling substantially weakens), raising uncertainty in future projections of Afro-Asian monsoon under continued warming and TPS loss.

title: National and city-level greenhouse gas inventories in developing countries: status, gaps, and pathways forward
abstract:
National and city-level greenhouse gas inventories in developing countries: status, gaps, and pathways forward 
 Accurate greenhouse gas (GHG) inventories are essential for tracking climate mitigation. While many developed countries now publish comprehensive and timely emission inventories, developing countries still face data, time and resource constraints that hinder inventory development. This paper reviews the status of national and city-level GHG inventories in developing countries. We outline the main GHG accounting methods and examine their application in developing countries. We then assess the uneven geographic coverage of inventories at national and city scales and analyze the challenges faced in these contexts. Sparse city-level coverage across developing countries reflects gaps in basic activity data, a lack of locally specific emission factors and inconsistent accounting boundaries that limit comparability. Additionally, many existing inventories are outdated and insufficiently transparent, limiting their usefulness for policy design and evaluation. Emerging techniques such as machine-learning and atmospheric-science based approaches remain constrained by data limitations, observation coverage and limited knowhow. Inventory improvement in developing countries should prioritize routine core data collection, transparent documentation, targeted sectoral and facility-level detail, careful evaluation of non-state data products and task-specific use of advanced methods. Sustained institutional capacity and long-term data stewardship are therefore central to closing the inventory gaps.

title: Projected weakening of Northern Hemisphere summertime high-latitude waveguide and teleconnection variability
abstract:
Projected weakening of Northern Hemisphere summertime high-latitude waveguide and teleconnection variability 
 Summertime high-latitude teleconnections shape persistent circulation anomalies and surface climate extremes across the Northern Hemisphere, yet their future evolution under anthropogenic warming remains poorly constrained. Using 31 CMIP6 models under SSP5-8.5, we examine projected changes in the high-latitude waveguide, teleconnection variability, and the resulting surface air temperature (SAT) response. The CMIP6 ensemble projects an ~20.3% weakening of the 250 hPa meridional potential vorticity (PV) gradient over 50°–80°N during 2050–2099 relative to 1965–2014. This weakening is driven primarily by the projected warming pattern itself: enhanced upper-tropospheric warming at low-to-mid latitudes together with vertically extensive Arctic warming reduces the meridional contrast in upper-tropospheric static stability. This weakened waveguide in turn supports less large-scale atmospheric variability. The interannual variability of the leading EOF1–3 teleconnection modes, represented by 250 hPa meridional winds, decreases by ~3.6%, with larger PV gradient reductions across models corresponding to larger declines in variability. This dynamical weakening does not, however, translate into weaker SAT variability. Teleconnection-related SAT variance increases because SAT anomalies become more sensitive to local circulation anomalies, although the physical processes underlying this enhanced sensitivity are not yet fully understood. These results show that the weakening of the high-latitude waveguide in a warmer world is accompanied by complex and diverse responses across multiple fields.

title: Metagenomic evidence for climate-associated variation in microbial methylmercury production across peatlands
abstract:
Metagenomes from 144 peat soils revealed higher relative abundance of the mercury-methylation gene but lower abundance of the demethylation gene at high latitudes, consistent with their opposing correlations with mean annual temperature, based on metagenomes from subtropical and temperate-boreal regions in China and metagenomes spanning tropical to Arctic regions. 
 Peatlands are major global mercury (Hg) reservoirs and are highly sensitive to warming, yet climate effects on microbial controls of neurotoxic methylmercury (MeHg) formation remain unclear. Here, we combined global synthesis with new measurements to assess climate-associated variation in net MeHg production. Metagenomes from 144 peat soils revealed higher relative abundance of the Hg-methylation gene hgcA but lower relative abundance of the demethylation gene merB at high latitudes, consistent with their opposing correlations with mean annual temperature. The ratio of nitrogen-fixation to denitrification genes (nifH/nosZ) covaried with hgcA and merB, suggesting links between nitrogen cycling and Hg transformation. Genome-resolved analyses further showed expanded denitrification pathways in hgcA-bearing taxa from warmer peatlands. Together, these findings indicate that warmer climates may be associated with microbial community restructuring and lower net MeHg production. A space-for-time framework therefore suggests reduced MeHg yields under future warming, informing Hg-risk assessment under the Minamata Convention.
